summary: PHP SDK's test framework doesn't automatically unlock time-skipping during getResult() calls, causing timer-driven workflows to hang in tests. The test server starts with time-skipping locked, and the SDK lacks the auto-unlock/lock pattern that TypeScript, Java, and Go SDKs implement.
userImpact: Users cannot effectively test timer-driven workflows because tests hang for wall-clock duration instead of fast-forwarding through virtual time.
rootCause: Two independent issues: (1) test server starts with Time Locking Counter = 1 (locked state), (2) PHP SDK lacks the implicit unlock/lock pattern around blocking client calls that other SDKs implement
proposedFix: Wrap getResult()/start() calls with implicit unlock/lock similar to TypeScript, Java, and Go SDKs, which automatically unlock time at the start of getResult() and lock it when complete
workaround: Manually call unlockTimeSkipping() before getResult() and lockTimeSkipping() after, though this collides with ActivityMocker causing activity timeouts
keyQuote: PHP WorkflowClient::start()->getResult() does no such thing... lockTimeSkipping/unlockTimeSkipping are referenced only in the README and generated protobuf — never invoked from Client/ or WorkflowTestCase
